final_proof:
Let \(X\) be the set of points and \(\mathcal B\) the family of blocks, where \(|X|=v\) and \(|\mathcal B|=b\). In a BIBD with parameters \(\{v,k,\lambda\}\), each block has \(k\) points and each pair of distinct points belongs to exactly \(\lambda\) blocks. As usual for a BIBD, \(\lambda\ge 1\) and \(k\ge2\); because the design is incomplete, \(k<v\).

For each point \(x\), let \(r_x\) be the number of blocks containing \(x\). Count in two ways the pairs \((y,B)\) such that \(y\ne x\) and \(x,y\in B\). Each of the \(r_x\) blocks through \(x\) supplies \(k-1\) choices for \(y\), while each of the \(v-1\) choices of \(y\ne x\) lies with \(x\) in exactly \(\lambda\) blocks. Hence
\[r_x(k-1)=\lambda(v-1).\]
It follows that \(r_x\) is independent of \(x\); write its common value as \(r\). Moreover,
\[\frac r{\lambda}=\frac{v-1}{k-1}>1\]
because \(v>k\). Thus \(r>\lambda\).

Now let \(M\) be the \(v\times b\) incidence matrix of the design, with rows indexed by points and columns by blocks:
\[M_{xB}=\begin{cases}1,&x\in B,\\0,&x\notin B.\end{cases}\]
The \((x,y)\)-entry of \(MM^{\mathsf T}\) is the number of blocks containing both \(x\) and \(y\). It is therefore \(r\) if \(x=y\) and \(\lambda\) if \(x\ne y\). Consequently,
\[MM^{\mathsf T}=(r-\lambda)I_v+\lambda J_v,\]
where \(I_v\) is the identity matrix and \(J_v\) is the all-ones matrix.

For every nonzero \(z\in\mathbb R^v\),
\[\begin{aligned}z^{\mathsf T}MM^{\mathsf T}z&=(r-\lambda)z^{\mathsf T}z+\lambda z^{\mathsf T}J_vz\\&=(r-\lambda)\sum_{x\in X}z_x^2+\lambda\left(\sum_{x\in X}z_x\right)^2>0.\end{aligned}\]
Indeed, \(r-\lambda>0\) and \(\lambda\ge0\). Thus \(MM^{\mathsf T}\) is positive definite, so it is nonsingular and has rank \(v\). On the other hand,
\[\operatorname{rank}(MM^{\mathsf T})\le \operatorname{rank}(M)\le b,\]
since the image of \(MM^{\mathsf T}\) lies in the image of \(M\), and \(M\) has \(b\) columns. Therefore
\[v=\operatorname{rank}(MM^{\mathsf T})\le b,\]
which proves \(b\ge v\).
